CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative evaluation for right knee replacement surgery scheduled for June 24th.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 76-year-old female with chronic CHF with diastolic dysfunction who presents for follow-up. She had an exacerbation of CHF earlier in the spring with increasing dyspnea. BNP was 3,000 in March and rose to 6,000 in April, prompting medication adjustments. Furosemide was switched to torsemide 20 mg daily, and lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily. Patient reports weight loss of approximately 3-3.5 pounds since last visit in April. She notes improvement in urinary urgency and attributes some benefit to oxyglutinine. She experienced bilateral leg cramps one night which she attributed to being cold from having ceiling fan on; cramps resolved with pickle juice. Denies current dyspnea. Breathing is non-labored. Patient is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th and wants to proceed with colonoscopy screening in the next 30 days due to upcoming insurance changes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current heartburn; previously had a heartburn exacerbation for about two weeks in January, treated with prilosec, which has since resolved. She is using the bathroom well. Denies leg or finger cramps currently. Lungs sound clear to auscultation bilaterally.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction
History of anemia
Diabetes
Hypertension
Scheduled right knee replacement surgery June 24th

MEDICATIONS
Torsemide 20 mg daily
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Iron supplement
Clopidogrel (to be discontinued one week prior to surgery)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of colon cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure normal.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, good air movement.
General: Non-labored breathing.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin: Normal (previous history of anemia, currently stable)
Potassium: 3.9 (holding steady on torsemide)
Creatinine: 0.7
BUN: 23 (mildly elevated, possibly indicating mild dehydration)
Magnesium: 1.7 (normal but below target)
Blood glucose: 169 mg/dL (non-fasting)
A1C: 5.5 in March
BNP: 3,000 in March, 6,000 in April; repeat results pending

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic CHF, mixed presentation. Patient had exacerbation of CHF in spring. Successfully switched from furosemide to torsemide; symptomatically improved with weight loss and non-labored breathing. Continue current medication regimen. Will repeat EKG today. Labs appropriate with good kidney function.

2. Pre-operative examination. Right knee replacement scheduled for end of June. Discuss need to discontinue clopidogrel one week prior to surgery; patient has written reminders. Schedule pre-operative check within two weeks of surgery (first or second week of June). May need to repeat EKG prior to surgery. No chest X-rays needed (recent imaging available). No additional blood work needed at this time. Patient counseled that colonoscopy will not delay surgery.

3. Colonoscopy screening. Overdue for screening colonoscopy. Will attempt to schedule within next 30 days at Bartley Regional Hospital given upcoming insurance changes. No family history of colon cancer. If results show 10-year interval, patient will be cleared for surgery.

4. Diabetes. A1C was 5.1 on last check; no A1C needed today. May need repeat A1C prior to surgery next month.

5. Hypomagnesemia. Magnesium level 1.7, below target of 2.0 range. Recommend magnesium supplement twice daily to help stabilize heart muscle.

6. Consider repeat fasting blood glucose given today's non-fasting glucose of 169 mg/dL prior to surgery.
